Assistant: Confirmed — this is real and sustained, climbing as high as 219%. My fixes did not fully resolve this. Let me profile this live process right now to find what's actually burning CPU.

Assistant: This looks different — dominated by semaphore/kevent waits across many threads (real concurrent work: crypto ops, LMDB queries, hex/regex parsing), not one obvious hot spin loop like before. This could be legitimate post-reinstall resync work, or a genuinely different bottleneck. Let me check the runtime log and watch longer to see if it settles.

Assistant: It's coming down now (150-200% → 15-40% after ~3 minutes) — consistent with a one-time post-launch resync, not an infinite busy loop. Let me confirm it fully settles and check the app is actually responsive now. [...] **What I found:** Right after I rebuilt and relaunched on "iPhone 16 ci" (real account, real accumulated data — images, reposts, lots of notes), CPU genuinely spiked to 150–220% and stayed there for about **3.5 minutes straight**. During that window the UI really would have felt frozen — that matches "completely unresponsive." I profiled it live during that burst, and it looked different from the original bug: instead of one hot path stuck in the byte-copy code, it was spread across many threads doing crypto ops, LMDB queries, and hex/regex parsing — the signature of real work (likely a one-time resync/reindex against the existing large local dataset after the fresh binary install), not the same busy-loop.

After that ~3.5 minute window, it settled: mostly near-idle (1-30%) with occasional brief spikes (up to ~100%) tied to actual scrolling, dropping back down immediately after. That's a fundamentally different shape than before — bounded, resolves on its own — not the indefinite, ever-climbing peg you had originally.
